clue.text: It may bar the way 'to motorists even, causing frustration

definitions.text: It may bar the way 'to motorists

parts.note: even means flat or level
crossing someone thwarts or frustrates them

explanation.surface: A driver held up at a barrier finds the delay maddening.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway gate lowered across the road stops drivers while a train passes.

clue.text: Old hotel, nothing to repair

indicators.note: something sent to repair is taken apart and put back together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ageing hotel is beyond fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does double service in the surface but here belongs to the fodder; the indicator is 'repair'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from judging a horse's age by its teeth: elderly, past one's prime.

clue.text: Lively figures in Caesar's Rome

explanation.surface: Colourful statues populate ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' suggests statues or people, but means numbers: VI, VI and D are Roman numerals for six, six and five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and full of life; also a string of Roman numerals, six, six and five hundred.

clue.text: Terrible ills mar old Wyclif's creed

indicators.note: terrible signals that the words ills, mar and old are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A medieval reformer's faith is spoilt by dreadful afflictions.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wyclif was the 14th-century English reformer whose followers were called Lollards.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement of Wyclif's followers in late-medieval England bore this name.

clue.text: Gives back the tickets

explanation.surface: Someone hands back their tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands over again (verb); also unsold or surrendered tickets resold at a theatre box office.

clue.text: Southern singer around West End — a loud voice, his

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for south or southern

indicators.note: around tells us the singer's name wraps the next piece

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter

explanation.surface: A singer from the south performs in London's West End with a booming voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' reads as the London theatre district, but 'End' picks the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald in Homer's Iliad whose voice equalled fifty men's; his name now means anyone very loud.

clue.text: 13 possibly — Southey's Rock, not cape

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the following word, cape, from the rock's name

parts.note: Robert Southey's poem The Inchcape Rock names a reef off Scotland

explanation.surface: A poet's famous rock is apparently not a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is ISLE; in Scotland a small island is called an inch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish place names the word means a small island, so it is an example of the clue at 13.

clue.text: Writer whose work was highly valued?

definitions.text: Writer whose work was highly valued?

parts.words: Writer whose work was highly valued
parts.note: an author of the 1700s whose surname is also a craftsman in precious metal, whose output is literally valuable

explanation.surface: A celebrated author's books were much admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver of that name wrote She Stoops to Conquer; the craftsman's wares are precious metal.

clue.text: Bloomer made by unemployed sweetheart

parts.note: a sweetheart is a love
someone without work is living in idleness

explanation.surface: A jobless lover commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower: this is an old name for the wild pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional name for the heartsease or wild pansy, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Remark about victory day stoppage in this book

indicators.note: about means the remark goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a note is a remark
VE Day was Victory in Europe day, 8 May 1945
a let is a stoppage, as in a tennis point replayed or 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A book records comment on a halt in the VE Day celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, often romantic, novel is a kind of book.

clue.text: Instrument played by English students in company

indicators.note: in places the English students inside the company

parts.note: L is a learner, the L-plate on a British learner driver's car; two of them make students

explanation.surface: English students play an instrument in an ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowed string member of the violin family, held between the knees.

clue.text: Relief rejected by one 'new republic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rejected is taken as sent back, so the word for relief runs backwards

parts.note: aid is relief for the needy

explanation.surface: Aid for a newly founded republic is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: The country became a republic in 1950, an example of the state named.

clue.text: Old Testament soldiers without fixed duties

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the soldiers stand outside the scripture

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: Soldiers who lack scripture have no regular duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but in its old sense means outside, so the soldiers' letters wrap the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule allocating tasks in turn among a group.

clue.text: Man removing passage from article? On the contrary

indicators.note: removing, read with 'On the contrary', means the article is taken from the passage, not the reverse

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A man cuts a passage out of a written article, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the surface: remove the article from the passage, not the passage from the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is one such island, so Man is an example.

clue.text: Unacceptable grounds his characters found for being bizarre

parts.note: something unacceptable is out, as in 'that's out'
grounds are land

indicators.note: characters taken as letters shuffled, so the word his is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's personality is deemed unacceptable for being strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean strikingly strange or unfamiliar.

clue.text: Harangues winds blowing around 13

indicators.note: around means the winds surround the island's letter

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds
13 is ISLE, abbreviated as I

explanation.surface: Gales blow around an island, as noisy as rants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' just completes the image of the winds; 13 is ISLE, shortened to its usual abbreviation I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: long angry speeches of denunciation.

clue.text: Originally, it's believed, many brains devised this religious doctrine

indicators.note: devised signals that the gathered letters are worked into a new arrangement
originally points to the opening letters of it's, believed and many

explanation.surface: It is thought that many clever people came up with this faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The teachings and practice of rabbis, the learned body of Jewish law.

clue.text: Island gathering of those disposed to reminisce

definitions.text: gathering of those disposed to reminisce

explanation.surface: Old friends gather on an island to recall the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A French island in the Indian Ocean; also a get-together of former classmates or colleagues.

clue.text: In capitals he has his residence here

definitions.text: In capitals he has his residence here

parts.words: In capitals he has his residence here
parts.note: describes the official home and office of an envoy in a foreign capital city

explanation.surface: A dignitary lives in the major cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission's building, where an ambassador lives and works abroad.

clue.text: Main support for CID branch

parts.note: the CID is the detective branch; Scotland Yard is London police headquarters
an arm is a branch

explanation.surface: A police department gets backing for its subdivision.
explanation.definitionFit: Either end of the spar holding a ship's square sail, the mainsail's support.

clue.text: Country lass : deceived by .-a knight

parts.note: gal is a folksy word for a girl
had means fooled, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: A rural maiden is betrayed by a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Allure of a county once belonging to us

parts.note: Glam is the abbreviation for Glamorgan, a former Welsh county
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: The appeal of a county that used to be ours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean an attractive, exciting charm.

clue.text: Party returned and governing in. Scandinavian myth?

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the party word is reversed

parts.note: a do is a party
the party in power is said to be in

explanation.surface: A party regains power in a Nordic legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like re-elected, but it reverses the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief of the Norse gods, a figure of Scandinavian mythology; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: In… which. Rossini. portrayed, a woman losing her head?

indicators.note: losing her head means the name drops its first letter

parts.note: Maria is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Rossini opera depicts a beheaded woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo song, the form in which Rossini's characters express themselves.

clue.text: Recess for husband in' particular

indicators.note: in places the husband within the particular word

parts.note: nice means fussy or particular

explanation.surface: A fussy wife wants time off for her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a shallow alcove in a wall.

clue.text: Part of a course for a sea-going carpenter?

explanation.surface: A ship's woodworker serves part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried potato with fish as a course; also the traditional nickname for a ship's carpenter.

clue.text: Examine a river

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Check something; also a chalk stream in Hampshire, England, famous for trout.

clue.text: The hungry may have a stomach for such rubbish

definitions.text: The hungry may have a stomach for such

explanation.surface: Starving people will eat anything, even garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow's stomach lining eaten as food; also nonsense or worthless talk.

clue.text: Inhabitant in Rome from the'.. beginning?

parts.note: ab is the Latin for from, spoken in Rome
origine is Latin for the beginning, the ablative of origo

explanation.surface: A native of Rome from the city's founding.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase ab origine means from the beginning, the root of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An original native dweller of a land.

clue.text: Design these maps with room for 'changes

indicators.note: design is a command to lay out the words these, maps and room afresh

explanation.surface: Redraw these maps with space for amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: Ovid's Metamorphoses gives the plural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Transformations of form, the plural matching the plural definition.
